headline: Native American Schools Hit Historic Graduation High
meta_description: Bureau of Indian Education schools reach 87-88% graduation rate, matching national average for first time in history.
summary_short: American Indian schools funded by the Bureau of Indian Education have achieved their highest graduation rates ever, with 8 schools seeing 100% senior graduation.
body:
Schools funded and managed by the Bureau of Indian Education have reached a milestone: their graduation rates now match the national average of 87-88% for the first time in recorded history. Eight high schools saw every member of their 2025-26 senior class graduate, while another 13 schools achieved graduation rates of 90% or higher. This represents a dramatic shift from 2015, when graduation rates for Native American students languished at just 51%—a gap that reflected decades of systemic inequity in education, healthcare, and economic opportunity across Indigenous communities.

The turnaround reflects a combination of practical reforms and corrected accounting methods. The Bureau of Indian Education modernized its data systems, equipping schools with pacing guides, instructional resources, real-time dashboards, and reporting tools that allow teachers to identify struggling students early and provide consistent instruction. Officials also addressed a historical accounting problem: previous statistics had counted students who changed schools as dropouts. Correcting this methodology revealed the true scope of student success.

Equally important were changes grounded in student reality. Remote learning options—adopted during the pandemic—remained in place at BIE schools to support students with family caregiving responsibilities or part-time work. Expanded vocational pathways kept technically-inclined students engaged, acknowledging that not all paths to graduation look identical. "These schools are a testament to what is possible when students, families, educators, and tribal communities work together," said BIE Director Tony Dearman. "Our students are showing the nation what Native excellence looks like." The achievement reflects not just policy shifts, but a fundamental reorientation: placing students at the center and building systems around their actual lives rather than forcing lives to fit systems.
quick_facts: 8 BIE high schools achieved 100% graduation rates in 2025-26
Graduation rates jumped from 51% in 2015 to 87-88% today
13 additional schools reached 90% or higher graduation rates
Bureau modernized data systems with real-time dashboards and instructional resources
Remote learning options kept working students and caregivers engaged
